fields.title: قصر ابراہیم
fields.summary: مٹی کی دیواروں اور کھجور کے تنوں کی چھتوں والا قلعہ، جو مسجد، سپاہیوں کی رہائش گاہوں اور برجوں کو یکجا کرتا ہے۔
fields.body: ہفوف کے قلب میں قصر ابراہیم (یعنی ابراہیم کا محل) صدیوں کی تبدیلیوں کا گواہ بنا کھڑا ہے۔ یہ عیش و عشرت کا محل نہیں بلکہ ایک قلعہ ہے، جس کی ایک ہی فصیل کے اندر وہ کچھ اکٹھا ہے جو کم ہی یکجا ہوتا ہے: نفیس گنبد والی مسجد، سپاہیوں کی رہائش گاہیں، نگرانی کے برج، اصطبل اور گودام۔ اسے خلیجی خطے کے روایتی انداز میں تعمیر کیا گیا: دیواریں بھوسا ملی مٹی کی ہیں؛ چھتیں کھجور کے تنوں، شندل (وہ لکڑی جو کبھی خلیج میں درآمد کی جاتی تھی) اور پتھر کی ہیں؛ اور مینار کے اوپر تک پتھر کی چکر دار سیڑھیاں جاتی ہیں۔ اس کے کشادہ صحن میں گھومیں اور دیکھیں کہ گنبد محراب پر کیسے سایہ کیے ہوئے ہے، تو آپ تاریخ کی وہ تہیں پڑھ لیں گے جو نسل در نسل جمتی چلی گئیں۔ آج یہ قلعہ الاحساء کے ورثے کے نمایاں ترین مقامات میں سے ایک ہے، اور اس شہری تانے بانے کا حصہ ہے جس نے 2018 میں الاحساء کے نخلستان کو یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست میں جگہ دلائی۔
fields.bestTime: دن میں، تاکہ آپ طرز تعمیر کی باریکیاں اور اندرونی صحن کی روشنی دیکھ سکیں

fields.title: العقیر
fields.summary: سعودی عرب کے مشرقی ساحل کی پہلی سمندری بندرگاہ، جہاں صحرا کی ریت خلیج کی نیلاہٹ سے جا ملتی ہے۔
fields.body: پکی سڑکیں بننے سے پہلے العقیر باہر کی دنیا کے لیے الاحساء کا دروازہ تھا۔ خلیج کے کنارے کی اس قدیم بندرگاہ پر کھجوروں اور سامان سے لدی کشتیاں لنگر ڈالتی تھیں، اور اسی کے راستے خبریں اور تجارت جزیرہ نما کے قلب تک پہنچتی تھیں۔ آج العقیر میں دو ایسے منظر ملتے ہیں جو کم ہی یکجا ہوتے ہیں: صحرا سے پھیلتی چلی آتی نرم سفید ریت، اور خلیج کی شفاف نیلاہٹ جو وہیں سے شروع ہوتی ہے جہاں ریت ختم ہوتی ہے۔ مٹی کی عمارتوں کے آثار اور پرانا قلعہ آج بھی اس جگہ کی نگہبانی کر رہے ہیں، اور آنے والے کو یاد دلاتے ہیں کہ یہ پرسکون ساحل کسی زمانے میں ایسی چہل پہل کا مرکز تھا جو تھمنے کا نام نہ لیتی تھی۔ یہاں تاریخ بھی ہے اور ٹھہر کر سوچنے کا موقع بھی: آپ اسی راستے پر چل سکتے ہیں جس سے کبھی قافلے گزرتے تھے، اور اس ریت پر بیٹھ سکتے ہیں جو سمندر کو چھوتی ہے۔
fields.area: خلیج کا ساحل، الاحساء کے مشرق میں
fields.bestTime: غروب آفتاب سے ذرا پہلے، جب سفید ریت پانی کی نیلاہٹ کے پس منظر میں دمک اٹھتی ہے

fields.summary: اسلام کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک، اور مدینہ منورہ کے بعد پہلی جگہ جہاں جمعہ کی نماز ادا کی گئی۔
fields.body: مسجد جواثا کو وہ مرتبہ حاصل ہے جس کی برابری کم ہی مقامات کر سکتے ہیں۔ یہ اسلام کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک ہے، اور کہا جاتا ہے کہ مدینہ منورہ کی مسجد نبوی کے بعد یہ پہلی جگہ ہے جہاں جمعہ کی نماز ادا کی گئی، جسے اس سرزمین پر آباد بنو عبد القیس نے ادا کیا۔ اس کی سادہ سی مٹی کی عمارت کا جو حصہ باقی ہے، اس کا وقار اس کے حجم سے بڑھ کر ہے۔ اس کی محرابوں اور دیواروں کے سامنے کھڑے ہوں تو نماز اور اجتماع کی وہ صدیاں آنکھوں کے سامنے آ جاتی ہیں جو الاحساء کے نخلستان میں گزریں۔ اس نخلستان کے لوگ سب سے پہلے اسلام قبول کرنے والوں میں سے تھے۔ اس مسجد کی مرمت “تاریخی مساجد کی ترقی کا شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبہ” کے تحت ہوئی۔ اسی منصوبے کے تحت الاحساء کی مسجد الجعلانیہ، مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا اور مسجد الحبیش کی بھی مرمت ہوئی۔ مسجد جواثا کی زیارت کسی عمارت کو دیکھنے سے بڑھ کر وقت کا سفر ہے، ایک ایسا لمحہ جو آپ کو اس جگہ کی تاریخ کی ایک گہری جڑ سے جوڑ دیتا ہے۔

fields.summary: المبرز کے قلب میں سات برجوں والا ایک بہت بڑا دفاعی قلعہ، جو یونیسکو کی فہرست میں شامل مقام “الاحساء کا نخلستان” کا ایک حصہ ہے۔
fields.body: قصر صاہود المبرز کے قلب میں کھڑا ہے: تقریباً 10,000 مربع میٹر پر پھیلا ایک بہت بڑا قلعہ۔ نگرانی کے سات برج اس کی چھ میٹر اونچی فصیلوں کی حفاظت کرتے ہیں، اور کبھی اس کے گرد ایک دفاعی خندق ہوا کرتی تھی۔ یہ بارہویں صدی ہجری کے اواخر میں تعمیر ہوا۔ اس قلعے نے علی پاشا کی لشکر کشی کے خلاف الاحساء کی مزاحمت کے واقعات دیکھے۔ اس کی فصیلوں کے اندر ایک مسجد، ایک کنواں، گودام، سپاہیوں کے کمرے اور اصطبل تھے، اور محاصرے کے دنوں میں شہر کے لوگ یہیں پناہ لیتے تھے۔ ادارہ ورثہ نے اس کی مرمت کی، اور آج یہ “الاحساء کا نخلستان” کے بارہ حصوں میں سے ایک ہے۔ یہ نخلستان 2018 میں یونیسکو کی عالمی ورثے کی فہرست میں درج ہوا۔

accuracy.why: 'Al-Ahsa's first formal government school' flat in both fields with the noun not widened («پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول»), 1937 in the summary and both calendars in the body, the same four places in the location sentences. Two points off: «شروع ہوا» is the Arabic's verb where the English says 'opened' (ruling P23), and 'stands on the rise' is now 'the rise it is built on is called'.

nativeness.why: The serious misreading is answered («اسکول»), and the sentence that lost him is his own two sentences now. Five points off: «تعلیمی بیداری» reads to him as an awareness drive, «نامی مقام ہے» is clumsy, «فرزند نسل در نسل» is bookish, «… اسکول ہے» reads as a school of today, and five edits in three leaves are unread.

compliance.why: «“بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام» exactly as rulings P3b and P15 build it; the year pair «1356 ہجری (1937 عیسوی)»; the hours cell with «اتوار تا جمعرات» and « · ». Two points off: four names of nine leaves are pending («مدرسہ امیریہ», «ام الخبیصی», «النعاثل», «بیت الثقافہ»), and a loan enters the text in this round with an entry no proofreader has read.

fit.why: The card was 'enough to plan with'; the common noun is now the word this reader uses for an ordinary school. One point off: he still cannot tell what the House of Culture holds (the source's) or read «ام الخبیصی» aloud.

structure.why: Nine leaves in pack order; labels «اوقات» and «فیس» are the approved pairs; 'Free entry' is «داخلہ مفت» as on qasr-ibrahim.

fields.title: مدرسہ امیریہ
fields.summary: الاحساء کا پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول، جو 1937 میں شروع ہوا؛ اس کی تاریخی عمارت آج ثقافت کا گھر ہے۔
fields.body: مدرسہ امیریہ الاحساء کا پہلا باقاعدہ سرکاری اسکول ہے۔ یہ پرانے ہفوف کے مشرق میں، محلہ النعاثل میں واقع ہے۔ جس ٹیلے پر یہ بنا ہے اسے ام الخبیصی کہتے ہیں، اور سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار یہاں سے قریب ہے۔ اسکول میں پڑھائی 1356 ہجری (1937 عیسوی) میں کرائے کی ایک عمارت میں شروع ہوئی، اور اس کی مستقل عمارت 1360 ہجری (1941 عیسوی) میں کھلی۔ یہ عمارت عرب اسلامی طرز تعمیر میں بنی ہے: دروازہ محراب دار ہے اور اندرونی صحن کے گرد برآمدے ہیں۔ اس علاقے کے فرزند نسل در نسل یہیں پڑھتے رہے۔ مرمت کے بعد یہ عمارت اب “بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام ہے، جو الاحساء کی تعلیمی بیداری کی یاد کو محفوظ رکھتا ہے۔

blind_reader_rulings.reason: Not a leaf of this batch: «یہ مقام محفوظ کریں» is the interface string fav.add, approved in batch b0-ui and so a pair of the translation memory. He recognised the Save button at the second glance. Recorded for the interface, not ruled away: batch b2's reader read it first as an appeal to protect the site as well (his observation 2) — two readers, independently, on heritage pages.

The notice is the template's (det.hoursNotice, ruled in b0-ui under P27). Part of the remark is an artifact of the plain-text page: on the built page «اس مقام کی انتظامیہ» is a link wherever the page has an operator link, which his page could not show. What remains is the source's: the notice names no channel (SD14 of the calibration), and on the mosque page it stands under rows that are the park's, so 'whose management' has no answer in either language.

The heading is the interface string trails.partOf (b0-ui); 'Trails' reads as roads or walking paths in the English too, which that batch logged as a source defect. On the built page the routes are listed under the heading; his page shows them as «⋯» because no trail has an Urdu title yet.

Both lines are interface strings of batch b0-ui (det.nearby.d, det.nearby.note): approved pairs of the translation memory and not leaves of this batch. The evidence is carried to the interface: «سیر مکمل کرنا» has now been heard as translated by three readers (b0-ui round 2, this one, b2's observation 3), and this reader and b2's wrote almost the same remedy («… جو آپ اسی سیر میں دیکھ سکتے ہیں»); both also faulted the qualifier that trails after the verb in the distance note.

An artifact of the plain-text page. The block is the home-page featured card: the kicker («تاریخی قلعہ», «بندرگاہ اور ریت», «نایاب ورثہ») is rendered there only and never on the detail page (pack, render_order: 'kicker: home-page featured card only'); the tool prints it after the back button. It is not a second category label of the page. Two pages have no such block because they are not featured.

The template prints the number of the World Heritage component bare after the label, in every language (logged by b0-ui: its two readers took 1563 for a year, a range, a code). Nothing in the page fields explains it and nothing may be added.

Neither source says who Ibrahim was, who built the fort or when, or how many centuries; 'stands witness to centuries of change' is the source's sentence in both languages. No fact may be supplied in the Urdu.

Applied where the wording is the Urdu's own: the body no longer makes the fort the agent that 'gathered' things; it says what stands within its one wall, in the frame of faq[3].a, which he read without remark. Not applied: his remedy dropped 'what rarely meets', which is the source's claim; and the summary keeps 'gathers' (owner ruling C39: its plurals show only in the oblique). That the page for «قصر صاہود» lists almost the same contents and makes 'rarely' ring hollow is the site's own contradiction: logged.

The explanation of chandal is the owner's ruled wording (build check C40: 'timber once imported to the Gulf'); it says neither which wood nor from where, and the roofs 'of stone' are the source's list. The misreading itself is recorded on the entry «شندل», which stays pending: built from the Arabic spelling, one letter from the Urdu word for sandalwood, and his bracket did put him right.

The sentence is the source's, picture for picture: 'watch the dome shade the mihrab, and you will read layers of history accumulated generation by generation'. The English also drops what the Arabic has ('you will read in its walls'), so the layers hang on nothing; an Arabic-only phrase is not imported.

Second point applied with his own wording, in the body and in the answer that stands alone: «اس نخلستان کو» is now «الاحساء کے نخلستان کو» (as the calibration page names the oasis once). First point kept: «شہری تانے بانے» is the image of the site's own claim ('part of the urban fabric that placed the oasis on the list', «نسيج عمراني»); a plainer word would change how the claim is put (ruling P25).

The best time ('Daytime') and the Friday hours (4 to 8 pm) are both the source's, in both languages, and the page does not reconcile them or name a season. «اندرونی صحن کی روشنی» is the source's phrase ('the light of the inner courtyard'). Logged with its harm: a visitor planning a Friday cannot tell whether it is a poor day.
His wording: «یہ عیش و عشرت کا محل نہیں بلکہ ایک قلعہ ہے».
The answer's second half (the World Heritage clause) is in both sources' answer, and the other three answers repeat the card in both languages (as SD15 of the calibration).
Neither source says whether the mosque inside the fort is entered or prayed in. Nothing is stated in the Urdu either way.

'First seaport' is the owner's ruled wording (build check C34), with no date and no sense of 'first' in either language; «سمندری بندرگاہ» is the source's own 'seaport' / «ميناء بحري». b2's reader stopped at the same two points on the sister page.

The label 'Hours & entry' stands over a value with no hours in both languages ('Open public site — no entry fee'); 'open' is as wide in the source. Whether one may come after dark or enter the buildings is not said and is not supplied.
'On the Arabian Gulf coast, east of Al-Ahsa' is all either source gives, in the card and again in the answer: no distance, no drive, Al-Ahsa treated as a point (logged by the Russian line too).
What a family would do there, whether one swims, the state of the buildings and how long a visit takes are in neither source.
His wording, whole: the idiom «نقش قدم پر چلنا» (to follow an example) is gone and the visit is said with «سکتے ہیں». That caravans arrive on a page that had spoken of boats is the source's.
His wording: «ٹھہر کر سوچنے کا موقع» for 'contemplation'.

The four blues are four places where the sources say 'blue' ('the blue of the Gulf', 'the clear blue', 'the blue of the water' twice), and the best-time line is the source's sentence; cutting it to «غروب آفتاب سے ذرا پہلے» would drop its content for a better register (ruling P24). «شفاف» is the common word for 'clear' said of water. One-line option for the owner, if the card may be plainer than the source: the first clause alone.

First point applied in his words («باہر کی دنیا کے لیے الاحساء کا دروازہ»). Second point not applied: 'the peninsula' is unnamed in both sources and the name he offers («جزیرہ نمائے عرب») is not in the termbase; on record with the reference title form «جزیرہ نما عرب» (768 pages) for a round that enters it.

CONFIRMED from the pack. The summary states the Friday claim flatly and says 'after Medina' in BOTH languages; the body and faq[2].a hedge it ('is said to be', «ويُذكر أنّه») and say 'after the Prophet's Mosque'. The Urdu keeps each field at its source's strength and levels nothing. The harm is the greatest of the batch: the flat version is the page's search description and card, on a matter of religious history, and it made the reader doubt the rest.

CONFIRMED from the pack. The park stands in two card rows and two FAQ items and nowhere in the body, in either language; the page gives no hours for the mosque (the owner's question on working mosques is open), and the price range has no explanation. Nothing is supplied: a family cannot tell from the page whether the mosque is open, or whether the park's fee is the price of reaching it.

'What remains' and 'was restored' are both the source's, with nothing between them; whether one can pray there is the question the owner has not answered, and the Urdu states no visiting time. The heavy sentence is the source's figure ('a dignity beyond its size'); stage 4 already took the amplifier out of it. Kept.

Applied in the body and in faq[2].a, but not with his wording, which would let the tribe clause be read as the site's own statement. A relative clause on the prayer keeps the tribe inside the hedge by syntax. That the tribe is not introduced as one is the source's ('the Banu Abd al-Qais who settled this land'); the Russian and Chinese lines added the word, the German did not; no generic is added here.
No year, century or period stands anywhere in the page's sources, for the building or for the restoration.

Applied for what is the Urdu's: the sentence no longer drops in on its own; it hangs on the oasis just named («اس نخلستان کے لوگ»). The strength stays the source's ('among the earliest to embrace Islam', «من أوائل من دخل أهلها الإسلام»): that it reads large to a Muslim reader is the site's claim, logged, not softened.
His wording: the project's name is marked off as a name, in quotation marks, in the body and in faq[4].a (ruling N16). «مساجد کی ترقی» is the project's own word ('Development', «تطوير») and stays.
Applied for the pronoun: the last sentence now names the mosque. The three sister mosques and their repetition in the FAQ are the source's, in both languages.

The sentence is the source's, image for image, in both languages ('a journey through time more than a visit to a building — a moment that connects you to a deep root of the place's history'), as is the opening. The register cannot be traded for the content (rulings P24, P25); the tone is logged for the owner.

Applied in the shape he and b2's reader both wrote: the row no longer hangs its conditions on «کے ساتھ» and no longer stacks «حرمت کے احترام». The source's nouns stay («اس مقام کی حرمت», not 'the mosque'). That it says no hours is observation 25.

The pointer is repaired (the oasis is named). «محرابوں» stays: it is the Urdu word for arches as well as for the niche, the plural told him which, and no commoner word exists. «اجتماع» stays: it is the source's word in its mosque sense ('prayer and gathering', «الصلاة والاجتماع»).
Both points: one word for the park in the label and both answers («ساتھ والی تفریح گاہ»), and the price range with «سے», as he wrote it (item N13).

The remedy settles open item P9, ruled in this round with both forms on record («مدینہ» / «مدینہ منورہ»): the epithet is written, in three places. «مدینہ منورہ کی» before «مسجد نبوی» stays because the English source names the city there. The card heading «سیاحوں کے لیے معلومات» is the interface's (b0-ui, ruling P27) and is carried to it with b2's same remark.

CONFIRMED from the pack. Since the owner removed the stale status row (2026-10-12) the source carries no hours, no fee, no FAQ and no opening status for this fort, and the body's interior is in the past tense in both languages. The Urdu asserts no status and adds no line. The harm: a family cannot tell whether they would be let in.

Item N14: the title is «قصر صاہود», the name of the place, and the labelled bracket is gone. What remains is the source's: the page has no sentence like qasr-ibrahim's to bridge the name and the fort, and never says who or what Sahood was.

Both sources give a Hijri century and no Gregorian equivalent; none is computed (site rule). The four notations he counts are four things the sources give: two calendars, one calendar, a bare inscription year, a century. The forms are ruled (N11, N12).
His order, the same words. Who Ali Pasha was and when the campaign took place are in neither source.

His rewording: no «اس مقام» before the quoted name, and the inscription in its own sentence, so that 2018 belongs to the oasis. The summary is left: it has neither fault. That a fort is a 'component' of an oasis 'site' is the source's vocabulary.

«بہت بڑا» twice is the source's 'massive' twice, in two fields each read alone; a grander word would add praise the source does not give (style rule on tone). He liked the paragraph for its plainness. Who the body is and when it restored the fort are the source's silences.

Item N15: the common noun is «اسکول» in the summary and twice in the body; the name «مدرسہ امیریہ» stays. The loan is admitted on all three conditions of the loan test, with the evidence in the calibration entry.

The defect is the English summary's ('opened in 1937' beside a body whose building 'opened' in 1941) and is logged. The Urdu summary takes the Arabic's verb («انطلقت»: started), a change of form under ruling P23; the body is clear as it stands.

What the House of Culture is and what a visitor sees inside is in neither source; the summary's lower-case 'a house of culture' is the source's. Two wordings kept: «نامی مقام ہے» is the frame of rulings P3b and P15, and «تعلیمی بیداری» renders 'educational awakening' / «النهضة التعليمية» word for word, no other word offered.
His rewording in two sentences; the hill's name now follows its generic. Whether 'east of old Hofuf' is inside or outside the old town is as open in both sources.
The fence: «بچے» would say children of both sexes, which neither source states ('the region's sons', «أبناء المنطقة»). The doubt he has is the source's own.

«تھا» would state that the school is no more, which neither source says: the sources name it 'Al-Ahsa's first formal government school' in an apposition without a tense, and tell the building's new use in their last sentence.

Settles open item P3c (the gloss in running text) together with item N14, both ruled in this round with their candidates. One name form for one kind («قصر X»); the «(عربی میں …)» bracket is gone; a name met in passing takes no bracket; two bracket forms remain, each with one job: «(یعنی …)» once, on a page's own name, and the bare meaning after a quoted institution name (ruling P3b).
Each page's sources word the listing their own way, and the mosque page's sources do not mention it at all; the badge is the template's.

Applied for the separator: one mark between day groups, « · » (item N8). The three ways of saying 'free' and the merged row are three source wordings. «شام 4 بجے» stays: 4 pm is a measured point of ruling P13 (20 pages to 1), and a ruling is not reopened here; b2's reader made the same remark, and both are on record as a one-line option for the owner («سہ پہر 4 بجے»).

The mould is the sources': 'rarely' on three pages, 'heart' four times and 'generation by generation' twice are theirs, page by page. «؛» is one of the marks of the style rule and stands where the source has a semicolon or where the parts of a list carry commas; the reader writes it himself in two of his remedies. One has gone with the hours cell (item N8).

Rulings P1 and P17, not reopened: «ہفوف» is the one name with a settled Urdu form without the article, and no vowel marks are written on a name. What Hofuf and Al-Mubarraz are to Al-Ahsa is the source's silence (SD10 of the calibration).

source_defects.where: jawatha-mosque summary against body and faq[2].a (observation 24, serious)
source_defects.defect: One claim at two strengths and in two wordings, in both languages: the summary states flatly that the mosque is 'the first place a Friday prayer was held after Medina'; the body and the answer say it 'is said to be' the first 'after the Prophet's Mosque'. The summary is the page's search description and its index card, and its wording is not the one the owner ruled (build check C30: 'after the Prophet's Mosque').
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each field keeps its source's strength: flat in the summary («مدینہ منورہ کے بعد پہلی جگہ …»), hedged in the body and the answer («کہا جاتا ہے کہ …»). The reader did not know which version the site stands behind and said it made him doubt the rest.

source_defects.where: jawatha-mosque practical[0], practical[1], faq[0], faq[1] against the body (observations 25, 26, 33, serious)
source_defects.defect: The only hours and the only prices on the page are those of an adjacent park that the body never mentions, in either language; nothing says what the park is, whether the mosque stands inside it, who pays 10 and who 15, when the mosque itself may be visited or whether one can pray there (the owner's question on working mosques is unanswered). 'What remains' and 'was restored' stand side by side.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Translated as it stands; no hours, status or explanation is supplied. A family cannot tell whether the mosque is open or what it will be charged.

source_defects.defect: Since the stale status row was removed the page says where the fort is and nothing else: no hours, no fee, no FAQ, no word on whether it can be entered; the interior is described in the past tense.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The Urdu asserts no opening status and adds no line saying that information is missing. The reader would not take his family on the strength of the page.

source_defects.defect: The English summary says the school 'opened in 1937' and that 'its historic building' is a house of culture; the body says classes began in 1937 in rented premises and the building opened in 1941. The English summary also drops the Hijri year the Arabic gives.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The summary now says «جو 1937 میں شروع ہوا», the Arabic's verb (ruling P23); the literal «جو 1937 میں کھلا» is on record. The body is unchanged.

source_defects.defect: A row labelled 'Hours & entry' with no hours; 'open public site' that does not say whether the buildings are entered or whether one may come after dark; 'east of Al-Ahsa' with no distance, in the card and again as the answer to 'where is it?'; nothing on what a family does there or for how long.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: «کھلا عوامی مقام» is as open as the source; the reader could not plan the trip.

source_defects.defect: 'Daytime' is the best time, and on Friday the fort opens at 4 pm and closes at 8; the page does not say whether Friday is a poor day, and names no season.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Both are translated as they stand.

source_defects.where: titles: qasr-ibrahim, sahood (and khuzam, muhairis in b2) (observations 38, 49)
source_defects.defect: title_en says 'Qasr Ibrahim' on one fort and 'Palace' on three others for one Arabic generic, and every body then calls its building a fort. Only one of the four pages has a sentence that bridges the name and the building.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: One Urdu form after this round, «قصر X» (item N14). The three pages without the bridging sentence still pass from a name that says 'palace' to a text that says «قلعہ».

source_defects.defect: 'Saudi Arabia's first seaport on its eastern coast': first in what sense is not said, no date stands anywhere on the page, and the English can be read as first in the Kingdom, which the owner's ruling excludes. 'Seaport' says the sea twice in Urdu as in Arabic.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The possessive ties 'first' to the east coast, as the Arabic does; «سمندری بندرگاہ» keeps the source's word.

source_defects.defect: No year or period for 'one of the oldest mosques in Islam'; 'among the earliest to embrace Islam' names no comparison; the tribe is not introduced as a tribe; three sister mosques are listed, and listed again in the FAQ, with no word on where they are; the opening and closing sentences are brochure figures.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Kept at the source's strength and in its images; the reader heard a sales tone that 'sits badly with a mosque'.

source_defects.defect: A Hijri century with no Gregorian equivalent; Ali Pasha and his campaign unidentified; the restoring body named with no date; the English drops the Arabic's 'military' and 'water'.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Nothing is computed or supplied; reading fast, the reader took the twelfth Hijri century for the twelfth of the common era.

source_defects.defect: Who Ibrahim was, who built the fort and when; 'what rarely meets' beside a sister page that lists the same contents; chandal explained as 'timber once imported' with no word on which or from where; the dome 'shading the mihrab' as a sight from the courtyard, and 'layers of history' that the English no longer reads 'in its walls'; an answer to 'what is inside?' that ends on the World Heritage list; whether the mosque inside is used.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Translated as it stands. «شندل» was read at first as a misprint of the word for sandalwood.

source_defects.defect: What the House of Culture is and what one sees there; whether 'east of old Hofuf' is inside the old town; whether 'the region's sons' means boys.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each kept as open as the source.

source_defects.where: World Heritage wording across pages; the badge (observations 6, 50)
source_defects.defect: The listing is told three ways on three pages and not at all in the text of the mosque page, which carries the badge; the badge prints a bare component number.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Each page follows its own source; the number was read as a year or a code.

source_defects.defect: The notice sends the visitor to 'the operator' and names no channel; 'Trails' reads as roads.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: None on this batch's fields: interface strings of b0-ui, logged there.

source_defects.defect: 'Free' is said three ways and one card merges hours and entry; 'rarely', 'heart' and 'generation by generation' recur from page to page; no page says what Hofuf and Al-Mubarraz are to Al-Ahsa.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The Urdu mirrors each source wording; the reader recognised the mould by the third page.

source_defects.defect: 'Arabian Gulf' and 'the Gulf' alternate inside one page; 'two rare scenes' moves the rarity that the Arabic puts on the meeting; faq[3].a moves 'old' from the fort to the port.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: The Gulf is bare in all eight places (ruling P5); the rarity follows the Arabic; the answer follows the English.

calibration.question: The gloss for a name whose Arabic generic is opaque or a false friend in Urdu («عین», «سوق», «قصر»), in running text: its form, and where it is owed.
candidates: A — the named gloss «(یعنی … کا …)» at the first body mention of every such name, passing mentions included (the text of stages 1 to 5)
B — the same form, owed only on the page whose own name it is; a passing mention stands bare
C — on a passing mention the Urdu generic in apposition after «نامی», no bracket
D — no gloss where the generic is itself an Urdu dictionary word and the page says in its own words what the building is
calibration.evidence: First pages that exercise the item. FORM: the reader met «قصر ابراہیم (یعنی ابراہیم کا محل)» and did not take the bracket for a second name (the calibration's finding on a bare bracketed name); he called the sentence that answers it useful (observation 13). SCOPE: the passing bracket on ameeriah stood in a sentence where he 'lost the thread' (observation 46), and b2's reader, on the same souq in passing, said the bracket told him what he could guess and not what the place is, 'the second (یعنی …) bracket in two sentences' (b2 observation 30). COUNT: this reader counted four bracket styles on five pages and 'kept having to work out afresh what each bracket was for' (observation 49): «(یعنی …)» twice, «(عربی میں …)», and the bare meaning after a quoted name. b2's stage 2 had already taken the bracket off a passing «قصر ابراہیم» under the ruled test 'by need', and b2's reader read the bare name twice without stopping at it. For «سوق» one reader of the interface batch missed a word saying it is a bazaar. Dictionary: «قَصْر — اسم، مذکر … ایوان، محل، بارگاہ» (Rekhta entry page, read again in this round): an Urdu word, in the sense the English titles give.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: One system. (1) A gloss is owed only on the page whose own name it is, once, at the first mention in the body, in the form «X (یعنی … کا …)»: the word «یعنی», the Urdu possessive, round brackets, nothing else. It is owed where the name's generic is not an Urdu word in the sense meant, or where the source itself glosses the name. (2) A name met in passing takes no bracket. If its generic is not an Urdu word («سوق», «عین»), the Urdu generic follows once after «نامی»: «سوق القیصریہ نامی بازار»; if its generic is an Urdu word («قصر», «مسجد», «قلعہ», «جبل») the name stands bare. (3) A «قصر X» name needs no gloss (ruling P3a's principle): the page says «قلعہ» in its own words, in the summary and the first body sentence, and never next to the name. «قصر ابراہیم (یعنی ابراہیم کا محل)» stays on its own page only, because the English source glosses the name there and its next sentence answers the gloss. (4) An attraction's own name (a page title) takes this form even when it is an Arabic phrase with a meaning («بیت البیعہ (یعنی بیعت کا گھر)», b2); ruling P3b, with its quotation marks and bare meaning, is for the names of projects, brands and institutions met inside a text («“بیت الثقافہ” (ثقافت کا گھر) نامی مقام»). (5) No bracket carries a language label: «(عربی میں …)» is not written. Two bracket forms remain for names, each with one job.
calibration.binds: Every attraction page: b1 (ameeriah loses its passing bracket) and b2 (baiah loses the souq's bracket; «بیت البیعہ» keeps its own; the two «(عربی میں …)» brackets go with item N14).
